subject: English
passage: A research team led by Omar Uwimana and Luciana Garcia uncovered fragments of a 900-year-old portable mechanical sundial at a caravanserai ruin along an old trade corridor in Central Asia. Little remains of the device except a bronze disc engraved with latitude markings and a hinged gnomon that folds flat for transport. Some scholars contend that the device was largely used by caravan navigators.
prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the scholars' claim?

choices.A: Other examples of the device dating to the same period have been recovered from the remains of several dwellings in the region, including one dwelling that may have belonged to a caravan navigator.
choices.B: Comparable timekeeping devices have been recovered from other sites dating to the same period that were linked to the caravanserai in Central Asia through trade.
choices.C: The other known examples of the device dating to the same period have been found along routes that appear to have been traveled primarily by caravan navigators at the time.
choices.D: Fragments of other imported goods have been discovered at the caravanserai ruin that probably also reached the location through long-distance trade.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it presents a finding that, if true, would most directly support the scholars' claim about the portable sundial. The text explains that fragments of a 900-year-old portable mechanical sundial were uncovered at a caravanserai ruin, and that scholars contend the device was largely used by caravan navigators. If the other known examples of this device from the same time period have been found along routes traveled primarily by caravan navigators, this finding would directly support the scholars' claim because it suggests that the device's distribution aligns with the movements of navigators who would have carried it for wayfinding during their journeys.
